articleTitle: A case study in curve design
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: An application of curve design to a material cutting problem is considered in order to help stimulate interest in geometry. Attention is confined to solutions drawing essentially on mathematics at A‐level/first year undergraduate level.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper suggests appropriate curves to model the volume of Easter eggs, apples and other three‐dimensional shapes found in nature. Whilst offering a practical method to find their density and show why apples bob, there are also extension ideas on how to develop this modelling to surface areas.

articleTitle: A graphical illustration of the limit of a composite function
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In first‐year undergraduate calculus courses, students learn the concept of the limit of a function and the various limit laws for calculating the limits of functions. publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Elementary ideas from fuzzy logic are used to formulate a simple model for social group interaction. The model is investigated for a simple social group containing three people. Ideas are suggested for further student investigation.

articleTitle: Mathematics for science: a Brunei experience
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper describes two courses developed at Universiti Brunei Darussalam for pre‐service and in‐service teachers who are trained to teach science at lower secondary level (ages 12–14). The courses are designed to focus on applying mathematics to solve science‐related problems. The content and coursework exercises aim to integrate mathematical knowledge, skills, problem solving, mathematical reasoning, and mathematical modelling at an elementary level. Details of the contents, sample exercises, students' responses, and modes of teaching and assessment are discussed.

articleTitle: AS Mathematics: The results of a survey of schools and colleges
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: There has been considerable debate about the problems associated with the new Advanced Subsidiary (AS) award introduced in 2000. There have been problems with examination arrangements, but there have also been concerns about the very high failure rate for AS mathematics, and the difficulty that teachers have faced in covering the content required in the time available. A survey of schools and colleges was carried out. This confirmed that teachers viewed the content of the specifications as being too much and that the examinations were inaccessible to many students. The paper also reports on entry patterns, the changes that teachers would like to see to the current system, progression to A2 and the benefits/disadvantages of the system as perceived by teachers.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: The study reported in this article deals with the observed actions of prospective Swedish mathematics teachers as they were working with a modelling situation. These prospective teachers were preparing to teach in Grades four to nine or in the gymnasium (Grades 10 to 12) and were students on a course in mathematical modelling. The way the students tackled the modelling situation, their strategies and attitudes are discussed as well as the difficulties in assessing mathematical modelling performance.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper describes a sponsorship workshop that can be run as the opening session of an introductory modelling course. Although knowledge of arithmetic and geometric progressions is helpful, students who are not familiar with these topics can participate by using a computational approach, with a spreadsheet instead of an algebraic approach. The workshop neatly provides a complete example of problem solving in a context, which is relevant to student experience, but which does not rely on sophisticated mathematics.

articleTitle: A first lecture in graph theory
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Here I look at a potential first lecture in a second year graph theory course. I believe that this type of lecture can provide an interesting introduction to a new topic that engages most of the students. It also provides feedback to the lecturer on the students' level of ability. But more than that, it recognizes that we all need to play with ideas to make them part of our knowledge pool and to increase our learning and understanding. Traditional lectures require students to sort out the basics of the subject for themselves. I believe that students don't do this well and hence need to be taught how to ‘play’ mathematically.

publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This article shows how integer‐sided triangles can be nested, each nest having a single enclosing isosceles triangle. It builds on work kindly published in this journal by the same author some time ago. It also brings to light what can be seen as a relatively simple generalization of Pythagoras' theorem, a result that should be readily accessible to many secondary school pupils.

articleTitle: Assessing children's mathematical thinking in practical modelling situations
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper reports on research into the development of mathematical thinking skills using practical modelling activities. An action research group of 12 teachers from six secondary schools in Wales was created to investigate the use of mathematical modelling tasks in years seven and eight (11 and 12 years old). Twelve intervention classes were matched with 12 equivalent control classes as part of a quasi‐experiment to investigate the impact of such activities. The experimental design was based on the use of written pre‐tests, post‐tests and delayed tests. However, in addition to the written tests, 48 pupils—two from each class—engaged in mathematical modelling tasks during one to one semi‐structured interviews with the researchers. The interviews used a form of dynamic assessment to analyse the development of pupils' mathematical thinking at each assessment point. This paper focuses on the interview data and reports on the extent to which some pupils proved to be naturally mindful and the extent to which metacognitive thinking might be taught in the early years of secondary school.

articleTitle: The introduction of graphic calculators into assessment in mathematics at the International Baccalaureate Organization; opportunities and challenges
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: This paper considers the impact of the introduction of graphic calculators into assessment within the International Baccalaureate Diploma. The difficulties, which arose in the development of practice questions, are discussed, as well as how these difficulties were resolved in the questions that appeared on the examinations. The problems of different calculator syntax are also discussed and suggestions for other examining groups are provided.

articleTitle: Compounding ratios and intervals: an educational approach in mathematics and music
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this study I shall consider educational aspects of the development of ratio and proportion, focusing on the arithmetization undergone by these concepts in the light of the relations between mathematics and music. Since such relations, even if confined to the context of ratio and proportion, are fairly wide‐reaching, and since the process of arithmetization is quite complex, we shall concentrate mainly on the instructional aspects of a structural peculiarity presented in such fascinating dynamics. This peculiarity is the so‐called compounding ratios, a curious feature present in the structure of ratio since the Classical period, whose irregular transformation into the operator multiplication is quite representative of the importance of theoretical music in the arithmetization of ratios. As a consequence, we shall also point out features of the differences between identity and proportion, which are capable of being didactically explored with a mathematical–musical approach.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling in the international baccalaureate, teacher beliefs and technology usage
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Mathematical modelling is perceived as one way of introducing more real life activities into mathematics lessons. This article investigates the introduction of mathematical modelling into the mathematics assessment programme of the International Baccalaureate Diploma. The article considers structured and open modelling in the context of this pre‐university mathematics programme. The influence of the use of hand held technology on mathematical modelling, as well as teacher and assessor beliefs about modelling are discussed with a view to the supporting of the incorporation of open modelling into the coursework components of mathematics education.

articleTitle: Developing transferable skills in undergraduate mathematics students through mathematical modelling
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: Undergraduate mathematics students should possess certain transferable skills upon completion of a degree. The Mathematical Association of America's recently published CUPM Discussion Papers about Mathematics and the Mathematical Sciences in 2010: What Should Students Know and the NCTM's Principles and Standards for School Mathematics both suggest the importance of transferable skills for success in students' later careers. These skills and a strategy for developing them via an intensive short course on mathematical modelling are discussed. Student reactions and comments on the course are included. The evaluation suggests that this course on mathematical modelling developed modelling as well as generic skills through the teaching, learning and assessment style.

articleTitle: Mathematics of a relay—problem solving in the real world
publicationTitle: Teaching Mathematics and Its Applications: International Journal of the IMA
abstract: In this paper, I will explain a useful application of mathematical modeling within a school setting, as well as a progressive use of graphing calculators in mathematical modeling. For the project, I used the concrete problem of baton‐passing in relay races, and analysed the students' performances in the process of problem‐solving. As a result, the following suggestions emerged. The students made effective use of their mathematical knowledge and ideas when they used graphing calculators in mathematical modeling. In this way, they were able to leave the door open to their decision making.
